page.layout: One block of running text in one column, with one marginal note on the left at the level of the line "quod desiderabilius". Page number and running head at the top. A catchword right below the last line.

main_text.p: dem reviviscant, nec victores ferunt inducias, nec observant victi. Inter Lyceū[?] igitur & Peripata vestra (Baccalaurei) vestra etiam alia Tentationum schola requirit exercitia, ubi non respondebit pro vobis Aristoteles, sed stipulatio bonae conscientiae, verbo illi innixa, 1.Pet.3; Pag.19.quod desiderabilius est auro & obrizo multo, dulcius melle & Favi fragmento. Vultis ut aliquod specimen huius doctrinae scholasticae vobis exhibeam? paucissimis sic accipite: Tentatio est militis Christiani Armilustrium, vel ad medelam vel ad ruinam. Itaq; duplex est (fuggerente[?] distinctionem Augustino) Probationis aut Seductionis. Ad probandum Deus ipse aliquoties tentat, idq; vel per res prosperas, ut Solomonem[?], vel asperas, ut Iobum. Seductio autem e contra tanquam laqueus injicitur per carnem, mundum aut Diabolum. Caro tentat, Deum, seipsam, alios: Deum, vel praesumptione, ad prodigenda vel pervertenda ipsius beneficia, vel concupiscentia, ad appetenda illicita: Tentat seipsam Caro, Socordia aut φιλαυτία[?]. Alios vero, vel malum suadendo, vel exemplum praebenda. Mundi deinceps Incantamenta, revocantur ad haec tria capita, concupiscentia carnis, concupiscentiam oculorum

page.notes: Left margin note "1.Pet.3; Pag.19." is placed beside "quod desiderabilius". Doubtful readings: "Lyceū" (the word is badly printed, possibly "Lycex"), "fuggerente" (possibly "suggerente"), "Solomonem" (line-end break, read as Solomo-nem), and the Greek word "φιλαυτία", which is hard to make out. The line below the text reads "oculorum", underlined and set right; it is taken as the catchword. The faint marks at the very foot are not text and were left out.
